title: Balanced Gaussian simplex noise stability for four or more classes
decision_reason: Exact source formulation, independent specialist corroboration, baseline duplicate screening, current resolution searches and a separated adversarial draft review support admission as an open problem. No matching later resolution located as of September 17, 2026.

problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: All measurable partitions modulo Gaussian-null sets; no smoothness or hyperstability assumption
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Partition covers space and is disjoint modulo null sets

statement_source_and_scope_match: The positive-correlation part of IM Conjecture 1.4, restricted to q>=4. HT Conjecture 1.6 with equal masses and w=0 corroborates this exact regime. No uniqueness claim is added.
proposed_statement_text: For every q>=4, n>=q-1 and rho in (0,1), does every measurable equal-Gaussian-measure q-partition of R^n have total rho-noise stability at most that of the centered regular-simplex cone partition?
applied_significance: For balanced classification of Gaussian data, noise stability is the probability that the label survives correlated Gaussian perturbation. HT §§1.1–1.3 relates this continuous extremal problem to noise robustness of low-influence voting.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Euclidean bubble perimeter is local, whereas this is nonlocal Gaussian stability at finite rho.
KLS is an isoperimetric bound for log-concave measures, not exact balanced multiclass Gaussian extremizers.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: One canonical balanced positive-noise simplex question. Discrete plurality reformulation, per-q splits and negative-noise variants will not be counted as additional entries.
implications_or_equivalences: HT §1.2 describes the invariance-principle relation to balanced low-influence voting; do not count both.
A rho->1 perimeter result alone does not prove the finite-rho inequality.
The weak simplex coding conjecture is not this Gaussian-partition conjecture.

open_status_evidence_summary: IM formulates the conjecture; independent HT preserves the balanced case and proves dimension reduction, while HYPER has an additional hypothesis. HEILMAN26 concerns only three classes.
independent_status_corroboration: Heilman and Tarter have no authors in common with Isaksson and Mossel. HYPER and HEILMAN26 share Heilman with HT and are not counted as additional independent sources.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Dimension reduction to q-1 dimensions; conditional q=4 result under hyperstability; recent three-class results do not settle general balanced q>=4 partitions.
source_access_limitations: Version/body-date discrepancies for IM, HYPER and HEILMAN26 are recorded above.
No full proof certification of the recent partial results or Mulgund claim is asserted; exact theorem scope was inspected.
